input.content:
# SMA-803 final whole-branch review

- Range: `0d24f914..41426fbf` (19 commits, code only).
- Authority: spec `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-18-sma-803-deferred-tool-calls-design.md`, plan Global Constraints and Review Focus, ledger `progress.md`.
- Method: `requesting-code-review/code-reviewer.md`. Read-only. No subagents.
- Passes. The diff is about 450 KB, so I did not read it as one file. I read it per file with `git diff 0d24f914..41426fbf -- <path>` in four passes:
  1. Core control flow: `agent.rs`, `context.rs`, `control.rs`, `permission.rs`, `tool_exec.rs`, `loop_state.rs`, `workflow.rs`, `graph.rs`, `swarm.rs`, `lib.rs`.
  2. Core state: `deferral.rs`, `resume_exec.rs`, `session.rs`, `runner.rs`, `compacting_session.rs`.
  3. Runtimes: `runtime-tokio/src/lib.rs`, `runtime-temporal/src/runner.rs`, the axum, actix and agentcore helpers and all seven build sites.
  4. Tests (selected: the pairing helper, the handoff and repeated-id runner tests, the review-focus test names) and the mdBook pages.
- I did not run `cargo test`. The per-task reviews ran the gates. My findings come from a code trace.

## Strengths

- The authorization change is clean. `authorize_stages` keeps the stage order, and the mark is applied in one place (`context.rs` `authorize_tool_detailed`). The flag-off mapping is one `match`. With a handler that returns only `Allow` or `Deny` (every handler that exists on `main`), the pipeline gives the same result and the same texts as `main`.
- The re-check reuses the same pipeline with `AskPoints::Answered`, so the two paths cannot drift. Deny wins on every exit. `Replace` with different args denies.
- Raw args go only to `DeferralSlot` and `ToolDeferred`. `ApprovalRequested`, `RunDeferred` and `StopReason` get the redacted copy (`agent.rs` deferral branch of `ExecuteTools`). `ResumePlan`, `PlannedCall` and `DeferralSlot` have a manual `Debug` that hides args.
- `ResumePlan` has private fields and only `from_events` makes one. The validation order matches the docs.
- `agent_view` strips every transfer call and every orphan result from a child view (`deferral.rs:574`). This removes the SMA-810 problem from the leaf request on the routing path.
- The recorder takes the resume block by position (before the first `TurnStarted`), and `drain` matches by position. This fixes the repeated-`call_id` cancel case (Review Focus 1).
- The strict-write rule is in one place per path in `runtime-tokio`, and `SessionWriteSlot` makes `run_streamed(..).collect()` give the same error as `run`.
- All seven HTTP build sites call `restrict_unsupported_run_features` directly after `build(..)`.

## Issues

### Critical

None.

### Important

**I1. A provider call id that repeats between a handoff transfer call and the child's deferred call loses the deferral silently.**

- Files: `crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/session.rs:664-677` (`drain`), `crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/deferral.rs:246` (`open_deferral_positions`), `crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/deferral.rs:407` (`CallNotInHistory` check), `crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/deferral.rs:574` (child-view orphan filter).
- Trigger: the Gemini provider makes `fc_{n}` ids per stream when the model sends no id (`crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-gemini/src/stream.rs:43`). The spec (§4.1) names this case. The root's transfer call is then `fc_0`, and the child's first call is also `fc_0`.
- Trace of a deferring run `triage -> budgeting`, where `budgeting` defers `pay`:
  1. The recorder stores `ToolCalled fc_0` (transfer, `loop_state.rs:308-311`). A transfer call gets no result in the run.
  2. It stores `HandoffOccurred`, then `ToolCalled fc_0` (`pay`), then `ToolDeferred fc_0`.
  3. `drain` keeps two unanswered `fc_0` calls. `ToolDeferred fc_0` removes one. The other gets the synthetic "tool call did not complete" result, appended at the end, after `ToolDeferred fc_0`.
  4. `open_deferrals` treats the deferral as closed, because a `ToolReturned fc_0` follows it.
- Result: the run returns `StopReason::Deferred { calls }` with a `deferral_id`, and the strict write succeeds. But the session has no open deferral. The host's resume gets `InvalidResume::NoOpenDeferrals`. The model sees "tool call did not complete" for `pay` on the next run. The approval is lost with no error.
- If `open_deferrals` were fixed alone, `CallNotInHistory` (rposition finds the `pay` call, then sees the later `fc_0` result) and the child-view filter (the `fc_0` orphan result is kept because a `fc_0` call is in the view) would still fail.
- Safety: this fails closed. No tool runs without approval. It is a correctness defect of the new feature, not a security defect.
- Baseline: on `main`, the same log shape (two `fc_0` calls, one result) already exists for every Gemini handoff run (SMA-810). The new part is the lost deferral.
- No test covers it: every test uses unique ids (`t1`, `call_1`, `call_b`). `repeated_call_id_does_not_match_an_old_deferral` covers repeats across turns, not a repeat between an open transfer call and a deferred call.
- Fix options (Sven's call, because SMA-810 is out of scope by decision):
  - (a) Pull the narrow part of SMA-810 forward: the recorder writes the transfer call's synthetic result directly after `HandoffOccurred`. Then the transfer call is answered before the child's calls exist, and all three checks work. This changes the log of every handoff run.
  - (b) Fail closed with a clear reason: when a deferring call's `call_id` equals an unanswered earlier `ToolCalled` in the run (the recorder can see this at `RunDeferred`), end the run with `RunFailed` or a deny instead of a deferral that cannot resume. Document it, and file a Linear follow-up.
  - In both cases add a runner test with a transfer call and a deferred call that share the id `fc_0`.

**I2. Public docs do not say which copy of the args is authoritative.**

- Files: `crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/agent.rs:528` (`RunDeferred.calls`), `crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/runner.rs:268` (`RunResult.stop_reason`).
- The spec (§4.4) says that `RunDeferred` and `stop_reason` carry the redacted copy and that the stored `ToolDeferred` is the source of truth for the host. The field docs do not say this. SMA-795 builds an args hash into the approval token. A host that hashes `stop_reason` args hashes `***` values.
- This is Task 2 Minor 2, raised to Important for this reason. Fix: one sentence on each field.

**I3. The mdBook says the event args are always redacted.**

- Files: `docs/book/src/concepts/agent-loop.md:66`, `docs/book/src/concepts/permissions-guardrails-hooks.md:114`.
- The code redacts only when output redaction is on (`agent.rs` `ApprovalRequested` doc says so). A host that turns redaction off and trusts the book sends raw args to SSE and AG-UI clients.
- This is Task 14 Minor 1 and 2. Fix: add "when output redaction is on" in both places.

### Minor

- M1. `crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/runner.rs:517`: `collect_typed` maps a lost write to `AgentError::Other("session write failed: ...")`. `AgentError::Session(SessionError)` exists (`agent.rs:1530`) and is the exact variant. After release, a change of the variant changes what callers match, so change it now (ledger Task 9 minor; cheap).
- M2. `crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/runner.rs:337`: `SessionWriteSlot::take` is `pub`, but only core calls it. Making it `pub(crate)` after release is a breaking change. Decide now.
- M3. Policy prompts are not redacted. `PendingToolCall.prompt` goes into `RunDeferred` and `StopReason` as the policy wrote it. A policy that puts args into its prompt (for example "pay {amount} to {account}") can leak a hook-added secret. The built-in guard prompts are static. The spec only asks for args redaction. Document it on `PermissionDecision::Defer`.
- M4. `crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/context.rs:383-391` and `:418-424`: the `handoff_child` and `subagent_child` method docs do not name the deferral flag, the handoff path or the deferral slot (Task 3 Minor 1, still open).
- M5. `crates/paigasus-helikon-runtime-tokio/src/lib.rs:159`: the finalize warning text lost "; run outcome unaffected". This changes the log text for every failed best-effort append. It is correct now (the outcome can change), but it is a visible change for log alerts.
- M6. `crates/paigasus-helikon-runtime-tokio/README.md:32` says nothing about resume, although `TokioRunner` is the only runner that resumes. The CLAUDE.md README rule asks for a conscious call. The book covers it, so a one-line pointer is enough.
- M7. `crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/agent.rs` `AgentInput::with_resume_plan` is public. A caller with direct agent access can build a plan from fabricated events and so get "answered" ask points. That caller already controls the agent's permissions, so this crosses no trust boundary. The doc says "a deferral-aware runner sets this"; keep it, but say that the plan bypasses the ask points.

## Focus 1: baseline regression (flag off, no resolutions)

Each behavior change I found for such a run:

1. Spec-required: `TokioRunner` and `TemporalRunner` read `session.events(None)` in addition to `snapshot()`. A failure of that read is a hard `RunError::Other` before the agent starts. On `main`, a custom `Session` whose `events()` fails but whose `snapshot()` works ran normally. Now every run on it fails. This follows from spec §4.6 step 1. I note it so that the PR body can say it.
2. `SessionRecorder::drain` (`session.rs:645-677`) now matches by position (multiset), not by a `HashSet` of ids. For a run with unique call ids, the output is identical (same synthetic results, same order, at the end). For a run where a call id repeats (Gemini `fc_0` across turns, or a transfer call and a child call with one id), `main` gave no synthetic result to the second call and left the log invalid. The branch adds the result. This is a fix, but it is a change in the stored log of a flag-off run. Name it in the PR body.
3. The finalize warning text changed (M5).
4. New empty span fields: `paigasus.deferred_calls` on `invoke_agent` and `paigasus.tool.resumed` on `tool.execute`. Empty fields are not exported, so OTel output is the same.
5. `LoopState::NeedsApproval` with any input now falls to the catch-all error text, not `not implemented: approval`. No driver reaches it (Temporal keeps its wildcard arms).

No change for such a run in: event set and order, authorization results and texts (including `AskUser` without a handler and guard `Ask` without a handler), `PreToolUse`/`PostToolUse` order, redaction (the refactor to `invoke_and_finalize` keeps the same hook input and the same final transform), the durable `execute_tool_call` path, workflow agents (the guard only fires on resume input), HTTP runtimes (the helper is a no-op when the flag is off), and `CompactingSession` (`open_deferrals` is empty).

`ctx.push_handoff_path` now runs at the start of every `LlmAgent::run`. A `PermissionPolicy` can read `ctx.handoff_path()`. No output changes.

## Focus 2: security

- Defer is never invoked: `ConcurrentOutcome::Deferred` skips `invoke`. A call to an unknown tool is not deferred (`unknown tool: {name}`).
- Flag off: `authorize_tool_detailed` maps every `Defer` to `Deny` in one `match`. `execute_tool_call` maps `Defer` to `Deny` always. `subagent_child` and `AgentAsTool` (`RunContext::new`) clear the flag. All seven HTTP sites and `TemporalRunner` clear it.
- Resume: `Denied` never runs. `Approved` runs only after `recheck_approved` gives `Ok`. Deny rules, guards, allow rules, mode and policy run again. The handler is never called. A missing tool denies. A renamed root and a missing handoff target deny every call. A workflow agent rejects resume input.
- Deny wins: a `Deny` from any stage returns before the mark is applied, in both modes.
- Args: the tool runs with `pending.args()`, which comes from the stored `ToolDeferred` (raw effective args). `handoff_deferral_round_trip` asserts the recorded args through a handoff, so the shared slot works across a handoff.
- Redaction: `ApprovalRequested.args`, `RunDeferred.calls[*].args` and `StopReason` come from the redacted event copies when `redact_output()` is on. The only raw copies are in `DeferralSlot` (hidden `Debug`) and the stored `ToolDeferred`. Gaps: prompt text (M3) and the docs (I2, I3).
- Fallback: if a runner does not wire the slot, the recorder stores the redacted event copy and warns (`session.rs` `RunDeferred` arm). A resume then runs the tool with redacted args. This fails safe for secrets but runs with wrong args. `TokioRunner` always wires the slot, and a test fails if it does not. OK for v1; it is documented on `with_deferral_slot`.

## Focus 3: pairing

- Root resume, no routing: the results go at `results_at`, the end of the snapshot, before the new input. Each `ToolCall` of the deferred turn is followed by the results of the calls that ran, then the resumed results. Valid.
- Routing (non-denial) on a recorder-written log. The re-review claim was: "the child's request has non-adjacent t1/t2 results". I checked the code, and the claim is **false** when call ids are unique. The leaf history is `agent_view(level)` (`deferral.rs:557-583`). It is `thread_handoff_transcript(parent view at k)`, which removes every tool item, plus `project(events[k+1..])`. The recorder writes the transfer results at the end of the log, so they are in the second part, but their `ToolCall` items are not in the view. The `retain` at `deferral.rs:574` drops each result whose call is not earlier in the view. So the leaf request has no `t1`/`t2` call and no `t1`/`t2` result. The root and intermediate agents only route and never call the model on this path. The claim holds only under a call-id collision, which is I1.
- Denial path (rule 1 renamed root, rule 4 missing target): `close_open_transfers` moves the recorder's transfer result to directly after its `ToolCall`, in the request only, as Ruling T8b-reorder says. It inserts `agent no longer available: {name}` only when no result exists. The depth and run-error routing exits close the transfers too (8b fix round 1).
- Ledger item "result at `at+1` may split a multi-call assistant turn": a handoff response records only the transfer calls (`loop_state.rs:308-311`), so a split needs two transfer calls in one response. The second one's result stays non-adjacent. That is the general SMA-810 case, which also exists on every normal later run on `main`. OK to ship.

- Deeper resume levels use core `project()` over raw events, while level 0 uses the session's `snapshot()`. A custom `snapshot()` override applies only at the root. The spec says to derive the split from the events.
- Release mechanics: whether release-plz raises `runtime-tokio`'s `paigasus-helikon-core` requirement to the new core version (minimal-versions build). Ruling T9-bump and the SMA-418 precedent cover it; not visible in this diff.
- Run-stream consumers that drop the stream early on a resume write nothing. This is the existing documented `run_streamed` contract.
- Provider acceptance of the moved transfer result (Anthropic and OpenAI grouping) beyond the structural pairing check. No live provider check was in scope.
- SMA-810 general non-adjacency of transfer results on normal runs.

## Strengths

- The authorization change is clean. `authorize_stages` keeps the stage order, and the mark is applied in one place (`context.rs` `authorize_tool_detailed`). The flag-off mapping is one `match`. With a handler that returns only `Allow` or `Deny` (every handler that exists on `main`), the pipeline gives the same result and the same texts as `main`.

None.

**I1. A provider call id that repeats between a handoff transfer call and the child's deferred call loses the deferral silently.**

- Files: `crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/session.rs:664-677` (`drain`), `crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/deferral.rs:246` (`open_deferral_positions`), `crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/deferral.rs:407` (`CallNotInHistory` check), `crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/deferral.rs:574` (child-view orphan filter).
- Trigger: the Gemini provider makes `fc_{n}` ids per stream when the model sends no id (`crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-gemini/src/stream.rs:43`). The spec (§4.1) names this case. The root's transfer call is then `fc_0`, and the child's first call is also `fc_0`.
- Trace of a deferring run `triage -> budgeting`, where `budgeting` defers `pay`:
  1. The recorder stores `ToolCalled fc_0` (transfer, `loop_state.rs:308-311`). A transfer call gets no result in the run.
  2. It stores `HandoffOccurred`, then `ToolCalled fc_0` (`pay`), then `ToolDeferred fc_0`.
  3. `drain` keeps two unanswered `fc_0` calls. `ToolDeferred fc_0` removes one. The other gets the synthetic "tool call did not complete" result, appended at the end, after `ToolDeferred fc_0`.

## Focus 1: baseline regression (flag off, no resolutions)

Each behavior change I found for such a run:

1. Spec-required: `TokioRunner` and `TemporalRunner` read `session.events(None)` in addition to `snapshot()`. A failure of that read is a hard `RunError::Other` before the agent starts. On `main`, a custom `Session` whose `events()` fails but whose `snapshot()` works ran normally. Now every run on it fails. This follows from spec §4.6 step 1. I note it so that the PR body can say it.
2. `SessionRecorder::drain` (`session.rs:645-677`) now matches by position (multiset), not by a `HashSet` of ids. For a run with unique call ids, the output is identical (same synthetic results, same order, at the end). For a run where a call id repeats (Gemini `fc_0` across turns, or a transfer call and a child call with one id), `main` gave no synthetic result to the second call and left the log invalid. The branch adds the result. This is a fix, but it is a change in the stored log of a flag-off run. Name it in the PR body.
3. The finalize warning text changed (M5).
4. New empty span fields: `paigasus.deferred_calls` on `invoke_agent` and `paigasus.tool.resumed` on `tool.execute`. Empty fields are not exported, so OTel output is the same.
5. `LoopState::NeedsApproval` with any input now falls to the catch-all error text, not `not implemented: approval`. No driver reaches it (Temporal keeps its wildcard arms).

No change for such a run in: event set and order, authorization results and texts (including `AskUser` without a handler and guard `Ask` without a handler), `PreToolUse`/`PostToolUse` order, redaction (the refactor to `invoke_and_finalize` keeps the same hook input and the same final transform), the durable `execute_tool_call` path, workflow agents (the guard only fires on resume input), HTTP runtimes (the helper is a no-op when the flag is off), and `CompactingSession` (`open_deferrals` is empty).

`ctx.push_handoff_path` now runs at the start of every `LlmAgent::run`. A `PermissionPolicy` can read `ctx.handoff_path()`. No output changes.

## Focus 2: security

- Defer is never invoked: `ConcurrentOutcome::Deferred` skips `invoke`. A call to an unknown tool is not deferred (`unknown tool: {name}`).
- Flag off: `authorize_tool_detailed` maps every `Defer` to `Deny` in one `match`. `execute_tool_call` maps `Defer` to `Deny` always. `subagent_child` and `AgentAsTool` (`RunContext::new`) clear the flag. All seven HTTP sites and `TemporalRunner` clear it.
- Resume: `Denied` never runs. `Approved` runs only after `recheck_approved` gives `Ok`. Deny rules, guards, allow rules, mode and policy run again. The handler is never called. A missing tool denies. A renamed root and a missing handoff target deny every call. A workflow agent rejects resume input.
- Deny wins: a `Deny` from any stage returns before the mark is applied, in both modes.
- Args: the tool runs with `pending.args()`, which comes from the stored `ToolDeferred` (raw effective args). `handoff_deferral_round_trip` asserts the recorded args through a handoff, so the shared slot works across a handoff.
- Redaction: `ApprovalRequested.args`, `RunDeferred.calls[*].args` and `StopReason` come from the redacted event copies when `redact_output()` is on. The only raw copies are in `DeferralSlot` (hidden `Debug`) and the stored `ToolDeferred`. Gaps: prompt text (M3) and the docs (I2, I3).
- Fallback: if a runner does not wire the slot, the recorder stores the redacted event copy and warns (`session.rs` `RunDeferred` arm). A resume then runs the tool with redacted args. This fails safe for secrets but runs with wrong args. `TokioRunner` always wires the slot, and a test fails if it does not. OK for v1; it is documented on `with_deferral_slot`.

## Focus 3: pairing

- Root resume, no routing: the results go at `results_at`, the end of the snapshot, before the new input. Each `ToolCall` of the deferred turn is followed by the results of the calls that ran, then the resumed results. Valid.
- Routing (non-denial) on a recorder-written log. The re-review claim was: "the child's request has non-adjacent t1/t2 results". I checked the code, and the claim is **false** when call ids are unique. The leaf history is `agent_view(level)` (`deferral.rs:557-583`). It is `thread_handoff_transcript(parent view at k)`, which removes every tool item, plus `project(events[k+1..])`. The recorder writes the transfer results at the end of the log, so they are in the second part, but their `ToolCall` items are not in the view. The `retain` at `deferral.rs:574` drops each result whose call is not earlier in the view. So the leaf request has no `t1`/`t2` call and no `t1`/`t2` result. The root and intermediate agents only route and never call the model on this path. The claim holds only under a call-id collision, which is I1.
- Denial path (rule 1 renamed root, rule 4 missing target): `close_open_transfers` moves the recorder's transfer result to directly after its `ToolCall`, in the request only, as Ruling T8b-reorder says. It inserts `agent no longer available: {name}` only when no result exists. The depth and run-error routing exits close the transfers too (8b fix round 1).
- Ledger item "result at `at+1` may split a multi-call assistant turn": a handoff response records only the transfer calls (`loop_state.rs:308-311`), so a split needs two transfer calls in one response. The second one's result stays non-adjacent. That is the general SMA-810 case, which also exists on every normal later run on `main`. OK to ship.

All new pub items are in `paigasus-helikon-core`. The runtime crates add no pub items (`restrict_unsupported_run_features` is private or `pub(crate)`; `Loaded` and `lost_write` are private).

- Root-level denial (renamed root, missing child at level 1) sends the full snapshot, including the child's tool calls for tools the root does not define, to the root model. This is the spec's design (§4.6, §4.7) and the same as any normal later run on `main`.
- Deeper resume levels use core `project()` over raw events, while level 0 uses the session's `snapshot()`. A custom `snapshot()` override applies only at the root. The spec says to derive the split from the events.
- Release mechanics: whether release-plz raises `runtime-tokio`'s `paigasus-helikon-core` requirement to the new core version (minimal-versions build). Ruling T9-bump and the SMA-418 precedent cover it; not visible in this diff.
- Run-stream consumers that drop the stream early on a resume write nothing. This is the existing documented `run_streamed` contract.
- Provider acceptance of the moved transfer result (Anthropic and OpenAI grouping) beyond the structural pairing check. No live provider check was in scope.
- SMA-810 general non-adjacency of transfer results on normal runs.

## Assessment

**Ready to merge: ready after fixes.**

The core design is sound and matches the spec. I found no path that runs a deferred or resolved call without approval, Deny wins everywhere, and a flag-off run behaves as on `main` except for the changes listed in Focus 1. Before merge: decide and fix I1 (lost deferral on a repeated provider call id across a handoff), and make the four cheap fixes I2, I3, M1 and M2. - Range: `0d24f914..41426fbf` (19 commits, code only).
- Authority: spec `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-18-sma-803-deferred-tool-calls-design.md`, plan Global Constraints and Review Focus, ledger `progress.md`.

- Passes. The diff is about 450 KB, so I did not read it as one file. I read it per file with `git diff 0d24f914..41426fbf -- <path>` in four passes:
  1. Core control flow: `agent.rs`, `context.rs`, `control.rs`, `permission.rs`, `tool_exec.rs`, `loop_state.rs`, `workflow.rs`, `graph.rs`, `swarm.rs`, `lib.rs`.

  3. Runtimes: `runtime-tokio/src/lib.rs`, `runtime-temporal/src/runner.rs`, the axum, actix and agentcore helpers and all seven build sites.

- I did not run `cargo test`. The per-task reviews ran the gates. My findings come from a code trace.

## Strengths

- The authorization change is clean. `authorize_stages` keeps the stage order, and the mark is applied in one place (`context.rs` `authorize_tool_detailed`). The flag-off mapping is one `match`. With a handler that returns only `Allow` or `Deny` (every handler that exists on `main`), the pipeline gives the same result and the same texts as `main`.
- The re-check reuses the same pipeline with `AskPoints::Answered`, so the two paths cannot drift. Deny wins on every exit. `Replace` with different args denies.
- Raw args go only to `DeferralSlot` and `ToolDeferred`. `ApprovalRequested`, `RunDeferred` and `StopReason` get the redacted copy (`agent.rs` deferral branch of `ExecuteTools`). `ResumePlan`, `PlannedCall` and `DeferralSlot` have a manual `Debug` that hides args.
- `ResumePlan` has private fields and only `from_events` makes one. The validation order matches the docs.
- `agent_view` strips every transfer call and every orphan result from a child view (`deferral.rs:574`). This removes the SMA-810 problem from the leaf request on the routing path.
- The recorder takes the resume block by position (before the first `TurnStarted`), and `drain` matches by position. This fixes the repeated-`call_id` cancel case (Review Focus 1).
- The strict-write rule is in one place per path in `runtime-tokio`, and `SessionWriteSlot` makes `run_streamed(..).collect()` give the same error as `run`.
- All seven HTTP build sites call `restrict_unsupported_run_features` directly after `build(..)`.

## Issues

### Critical

None.

### Important

**I1. A provider call id that repeats between a handoff transfer call and the child's deferred call loses the deferral silently.**

- Files: `crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/session.rs:664-677` (`drain`), `crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/deferral.rs:246` (`open_deferral_positions`), `crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/deferral.rs:407` (`CallNotInHistory` check), `crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/deferral.rs:574` (child-view orphan filter).
- Trigger: the Gemini provider makes `fc_{n}` ids per stream when the model sends no id (`crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-gemini/src/stream.rs:43`). The spec (§4.1) names this case. The root's transfer call is then `fc_0`, and the child's first call is also `fc_0`.
- Trace of a deferring run `triage -> budgeting`, where `budgeting` defers `pay`:
  1. The recorder stores `ToolCalled fc_0` (transfer, `loop_state.rs:308-311`). A transfer call gets no result in the run.
  2. It stores `HandoffOccurred`, then `ToolCalled fc_0` (`pay`), then `ToolDeferred fc_0`.
  3. `drain` keeps two unanswered `fc_0` calls. `ToolDeferred fc_0` removes one. The other gets the synthetic "tool call did not complete" result, appended at the end, after `ToolDeferred fc_0`.
  4. `open_deferrals` treats the deferral as closed, because a `ToolReturned fc_0` follows it.
- Result: the run returns `StopReason::Deferred { calls }` with a `deferral_id`, and the strict write succeeds. But the session has no open deferral. The host's resume gets `InvalidResume::NoOpenDeferrals`. The model sees "tool call did not complete" for `pay` on the next run. The approval is lost with no error.

That caller already controls the agent's permissions, so this crosses no trust boundary. The doc says "a deferral-aware runner sets this"; keep it, but say that the plan bypasses the ask points.

## Focus 1: baseline regression (flag off, no resolutions)

Each behavior change I found for such a run:

1. Spec-required: `TokioRunner` and `TemporalRunner` read `session.events(None)` in addition to `snapshot()`. A failure of that read is a hard `RunError::Other` before the agent starts. On `main`, a custom `Session` whose `events()` fails but whose `snapshot()` works ran normally. Now every run on it fails. This follows from spec §4.6 step 1. I note it so that the PR body can say it.
2. `SessionRecorder::drain` (`session.rs:645-677`) now matches by position (multiset), not by a `HashSet` of ids. For a run with unique call ids, the output is identical (same synthetic results, same order, at the end). For a run where a call id repeats (Gemini `fc_0` across turns, or a transfer call and a child call with one id), `main` gave no synthetic result to the second call and left the log invalid. The branch adds the result. This is a fix, but it is a change in the stored log of a flag-off run. Name it in the PR body.
3. The finalize warning text changed (M5).
4. New empty span fields: `paigasus.deferred_calls` on `invoke_agent` and `paigasus.tool.resumed` on `tool.execute`. Empty fields are not exported, so OTel output is the same.
5. `LoopState::NeedsApproval` with any input now falls to the catch-all error text, not `not implemented: approval`. No driver reaches it (Temporal keeps its wildcard arms).

No change for such a run in: event set and order, authorization results and texts (including `AskUser` without a handler and guard `Ask` without a handler), `PreToolUse`/`PostToolUse` order, redaction (the refactor to `invoke_and_finalize` keeps the same hook input and the same final transform), the durable `execute_tool_call` path, workflow agents (the guard only fires on resume input), HTTP runtimes (the helper is a no-op when the flag is off), and `CompactingSession` (`open_deferrals` is empty).

`ctx.push_handoff_path` now runs at the start of every `LlmAgent::run`. A `PermissionPolicy` can read `ctx.handoff_path()`. No output changes.

## Focus 2: security

- Defer is never invoked: `ConcurrentOutcome::Deferred` skips `invoke`. A call to an unknown tool is not deferred (`unknown tool: {name}`).
- Flag off: `authorize_tool_detailed` maps every `Defer` to `Deny` in one `match`. `execute_tool_call` maps `Defer` to `Deny` always. `subagent_child` and `AgentAsTool` (`RunContext::new`) clear the flag. All seven HTTP sites and `TemporalRunner` clear it.
- Resume: `Denied` never runs. `Approved` runs only after `recheck_approved` gives `Ok`. Deny rules, guards, allow rules, mode and policy run again. The handler is never called. A missing tool denies. A renamed root and a missing handoff target deny every call. A workflow agent rejects resume input.
- Deny wins: a `Deny` from any stage returns before the mark is applied, in both modes.
- Args: the tool runs with `pending.args()`, which comes from the stored `ToolDeferred` (raw effective args). `handoff_deferral_round_trip` asserts the recorded args through a handoff, so the shared slot works across a handoff.
- Redaction: `ApprovalRequested.args`, `RunDeferred.calls[*].args` and `StopReason` come from the redacted event copies when `redact_output()` is on. The only raw copies are in `DeferralSlot` (hidden `Debug`) and the stored `ToolDeferred`. Gaps: prompt text (M3) and the docs (I2, I3).
- Fallback: if a runner does not wire the slot, the recorder stores the redacted event copy and warns (`session.rs` `RunDeferred` arm). A resume then runs the tool with redacted args. This fails safe for secrets but runs with wrong args. `TokioRunner` always wires the slot, and a test fails if it does not. OK for v1; it is documented on `with_deferral_slot`.

## Focus 3: pairing

- Root resume, no routing: the results go at `results_at`, the end of the snapshot, before the new input. Each `ToolCall` of the deferred turn is followed by the results of the calls that ran, then the resumed results. Valid.
- Routing (non-denial) on a recorder-written log. The re-review claim was: "the child's request has non-adjacent t1/t2 results". I checked the code, and the claim is **false** when call ids are unique. The leaf history is `agent_view(level)` (`deferral.rs:557-583`). It is `thread_handoff_transcript(parent view at k)`, which removes every tool item, plus `project(events[k+1..])`. The recorder writes the transfer results at the end of the log, so they are in the second part, but their `ToolCall` items are not in the view. The `retain` at `deferral.rs:574` drops each result whose call is not earlier in the view. So the leaf request has no `t1`/`t2` call and no `t1`/`t2` result. The root and intermediate agents only route and never call the model on this path. The claim holds only under a call-id collision, which is I1.
- Denial path (rule 1 renamed root, rule 4 missing target): `close_open_transfers` moves the recorder's transfer result to directly after its `ToolCall`, in the request only, as Ruling T8b-reorder says. It inserts `agent no longer available: {name}` only when no result exists. The depth and run-error routing exits close the transfers too (8b fix round 1).
- Ledger item "result at `at+1` may split a multi-call assistant turn": a handoff response records only the transfer calls (`loop_state.rs:308-311`), so a split needs two transfer calls in one response. The second one's result stays non-adjacent. That is the general SMA-810 case, which also exists on every normal later run on `main`. OK to ship.

## Focus 4: public API surface

All new pub items are in `paigasus-helikon-core`. The runtime crates add no pub items (`restrict_unsupported_run_features` is private or `pub(crate)`; `Loaded` and `lost_write` are private).

## Focus 5: consistency

- Texts match the Global Constraints list: `permission denied: {reason}` (`agent.rs`, `resume_exec.rs`, `tool_exec.rs`), `agent no longer available: {name}` (`agent.rs`, `resume_exec.rs`), `tool no longer available: {name}`, `arguments changed on re-check`, `tool call did not run: the run ended before the resume completed`, `resolutions require a deferral-aware runner`, `this agent cannot resume deferred calls` (5 agents), `approval deferred, but this run cannot defer: {prompt}` (`context.rs`, `tool_exec.rs`, book). One extra text outside the list: `approval deferred again on re-check` (`resume_exec.rs`, unreachable, fail-closed). OK.

## Declined to judge

- Root-level denial (renamed root, missing child at level 1) sends the full snapshot, including the child's tool calls for tools the root does not define, to the root model. This is the spec's design (§4.6, §4.7) and the same as any normal later run on `main`.
- Deeper resume levels use core `project()` over raw events, while level 0 uses the session's `snapshot()`. A custom `snapshot()` override applies only at the root. The spec says to derive the split from the events.
- Release mechanics: whether release-plz raises `runtime-tokio`'s `paigasus-helikon-core` requirement to the new core version (minimal-versions build). Ruling T9-bump and the SMA-418 precedent cover it; not visible in this diff.
- Run-stream consumers that drop the stream early on a resume write nothing. This is the existing documented `run_streamed` contract.
- Provider acceptance of the moved transfer result (Anthropic and OpenAI grouping) beyond the structural pairing check. No live provider check was in scope.
- SMA-810 general non-adjacency of transfer results on normal runs.

## Assessment

**Ready to merge: ready after fixes.**

The core design is sound and matches the spec. I found no path that runs a deferred or resolved call without approval, Deny wins everywhere, and a flag-off run behaves as on `main` except for the changes listed in Focus 1. Before merge: decide and fix I1 (lost deferral on a repeated provider call id across a handoff), and make the four cheap fixes I2, I3, M1 and M2. Name the two Focus 1 behavior changes (the hard `events()` read failure and the position-based drain) in the PR body.
